judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eminent-domain risk narrative; descriptive and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No contrary provision elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list-stem that says the Company 'may be limited by law or by the terms of its loan agreement, including without limitation with respect to the following' — an open-ended catch-all introducing enumerated items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'its loan agreement' is singular and undefined; the operative borrowing provision is c108's 'Company Borrowing', so the referent is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Diversification risk narrative; hedged but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c077 imposes a 20% per-loan limit only 'after the second year of the Company's term', so this risk is real in the early period; that is disclosure, not conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Portfolio Loans will generally not be personal obligations of the applicable borrowers' is an assertion about loan terms embedded in a risk factor, hedged by 'generally'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c066 contemplates considering a guarantor's creditworthiness, which sits uneasily with loans that are not personal obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A Project will be released as collateral as it is sold and the payment is made on the Portfolio Loan' states a release mechanic as fact within a risk factor, without specifying the release condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No release covenant appears in Section IV's lending criteria, so this is the only statement of the mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Although the Company intends to require its Portfolio Borrowers to maintain adequate insurance' is an intention, not an obligation, and 'adequate' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c069 makes satisfactory fire and casualty insurance an escrow condition naming the Company as loss payee for the full loan amount, which is firmer than this 'intends to require' framing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long mezzanine-risk narrative; technical but each step is expressed conditionally and clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates raising capital 'from Noteholders or new investors' to buy senior notes, which fits c019 and c091 without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describes a pledge-of-equity structure and its consequences; conditional but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A loan secured by an equity pledge rather than a deed of trust is hard to square with c060's statement that the Company makes loans 'secured by deeds of trust' and with the c061 loan-to-value table.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commercially reasonable efforts in reliance on qualified advisors' is a soft standard, though standard in risk disclosure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeats c133's formulation almost verbatim; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Usury risk narrative directed at Portfolio Loans; clearly bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c132 raises the converse risk that the Notes themselves may be usurious against the Company; the two halves of the usury discussion are complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A non-exhaustive list stem ('include, but are not limited to, the following'); no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to Section III Conflicts of Interest, which it summarises accurately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Time-demand conflict narrative; hedged but nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c056 and c110 on the Manager's time commitment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'Proportionally Disproportionate Interest of Manager' is self-contradictory phrasing, and 'Company gains and certain other income' is vague about what the Manager receives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes the Manager and its members receiving 'Company gains', which is in tension with c112's statement that all tax items are allocated to Members and with c100/c101's specification of the Manager's compensation as fees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conflict-of-interest narrative closing with an entrustment statement; broad but expressly non-exhaustive and plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c048-c059 and c156.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list stem describing the Notes as subject to risks 'typical of investments in private equity funds', which sits oddly with a debt instrument but is only framing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c018 and c123 insist the Notes are debt and not equity, so characterising the investment as private-equity-like is a mild internal dissonance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company will begin operations upon closing. It has no operating history' — plain and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c026's disclaimer; c022-c025's track record is expressly about affiliates, not the Company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concentration risk narrative; descriptive only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c077's diversification covenant applies only after the second year, which this disclosure implicitly acknowledges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blind-pool risk narrative; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c167's passive-investment description.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concedes there is 'no assurance that the Noteholders' security interest will be perfected in seniority', which is a candid but sweeping qualification of the security promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly qualifies c012 and c018's statements that the Notes are secured by the Company's assets and that Noteholders are secured creditors, and depends on c108's pre-authorised senior liens.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'severely restricted' is an imprecise characterisation, but this is a one-sentence risk factor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c107 permits certain transfers to family trusts and wholly-owned affiliates, which this absolute-sounding statement omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Noteholders will bear the economic risks of their investment until the Notes are paid in full' is clear; the investment-intent representation is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c094 and c017 allow a discretionary prepayment request after a year, which qualifies 'until the Notes are paid in full' only mildly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'precludes the Noteholders from active participation... or from voting on Company operating matters' is stated as an absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c109 and c114 give Noteholders a Majority in Interest veto over merger, liens, salaries and amendments, and c095 gives consent rights over the Collateral Agent — a direct contradiction of 'precludes... voting on Company operating matters'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Decisions with respect to the management of the Company will be made by the Principals' is flat, while the rest of the document vests management in the Manager entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c084 and c027 place management in the Manager, with the Principals merely its owners; c084 also allows substitute managers, which this provision does not contemplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Advisory risk factor with cross-references; 'certain defenses' is vague but the passage is plainly disclosure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c128-c134.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Coins 'the Company Act' as shorthand for the Investment Company Act of 1940, a label that invites confusion with the 'Company Agreement' and 'the Company' used throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c003 calls the same statute the 'Investment Company Act', c130 does the same, and c176 calls it 'the Companies Act' — three labels for one statute across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closing disclaimer; 'no assurance' language is definite in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c026, c135 and c161.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Interest Roll-over Request' is capitalised as a defined term here but c089 defines only 'Roll-over Interest'; otherwise the eligibility requirement is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c089 permits reinvestment 'provided that the Noteholder is a qualified investor at the time of the making of the request', which matches this requirement in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stem introducing the accredited-investor tests by reference to Rule 501; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The sub-clauses that follow depart from Rule 501 in places (notably c175), so the incorporation is imperfect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks Rule 501's individual tests closely with specific dollar thresholds; the 'reasonable expectation of reaching the same income level' clause is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c088's general accredited-investor reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limits the trust category to an 'IRREVOCABLE TRUST', whereas Rule 501(a)(7) requires only a trust not formed for the specific purpose with a sophisticated purchaser-director — a narrowing that does not match the rule it purports to track.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c179 separately qualifies 'a living trust or other revocable trust' whose grantors and trustees are accredited, so the instrument treats revocable trusts inconsistently across two clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to an 'INVESTMENT COMPANY registered under the United States Companies Act of 1940' — there is no 'Companies Act of 1940'; the intended statute is the Investment Company Act.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c003, c130 and c170 name the same statute differently again; the mislabelled defined term here would govern which entities qualify.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'gither (A)... or (B)' is an OCR slip for 'either', and the (B) branch runs two alternatives together ('total assets in excess of $5,000,000 or, if such plan is a self-directed plan...') so the structure is hard to parse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in substance with Rule 501(a)(1) as incorporated by c173.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'not formed for the purpose of acquiring the Note... in each case with total assets in excess of $5,000,000' is clear, though the $5,000,000 test applies to the 501(c)(3) organisation too.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c180 addresses entities that were formed to purchase a Note, so the two clauses cover the field together without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The self-referential 'qualify under clause (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) or (v) above or this clause (vi)' creates a circular look-through with no stated limit on iterations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It admits revocable and living trusts by look-through while c175 admits only irrevocable trusts directly — the two clauses pull in different directions on trust eligibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean look-through requirement for purpose-formed entities keyed to clauses (i)-(vi).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c178 excludes purpose-formed entities from clause (v), and this provision supplies the alternative route; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard investment-intent representation with a specific no-arrangement covenant; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c004, c107 and c166.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'such knowledge and experience... capable of evaluating the merits and risks' is a familiar but inherently qualitative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c173 and c129; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sole and absolute discretion' to accept or reject 'all or a portion' of a subscription is one-sided but unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c005, c088, c091 and c092.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'without unreasonable effort or expense' is a soft qualifier on the information obligation, but the clause is otherwise a standard Reg D access provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeats c007 nearly verbatim; c111 limits ongoing reporting to the Manager's discretion, which applies post-closing rather than to this pre-closing right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to 'its Managing Member' — a term never defined anywhere in the instrument — and declares the Summary of Principal Terms 'necessarily incomplete' and wholly subordinate to an unseen agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c081 uses the same undefined 'Managing Member', while c084 and c097 make clear the Manager is The Mortgage Fund LLC; and this qualification subordinates the entire Section V summary, including the c089 payment terms, to a document not before the investor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A contact block; no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c184's direction that questions be put to the Principals.
